s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The IMF and IBRD were founded in 1944. The IMF formally came into existence on 27 December 1945, began operations on 1 March 1947, and France was its first borrower on 8 May 1947.

s: Which arrangement filled the gap left by the never-created International Trade Organization from 1947 until 1995?
x: The ITO proposed at Bretton Woods was not created; GATT filled the gap from 1947 until the WTO was set up in 1995.

s: For about how long did the Smithsonian Agreement of 1971, which replaced the Bretton Woods parities, last?
x: The Smithsonian Agreement lasted only about 14 months, not 14 years.

s: Where is the headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) located?
x: The IMF and the World Bank are both headquartered in Washington, D.C. The WTO is in Geneva.

s: Which of the following is true of India's membership of the IMF and IBRD?
o: Joined the IBRD as a founding member but joined the IMF later
Was not a member of either institution at their founding
Joined the IMF in 1947 but not the IBRD
Joined both as a founding member
x: India was a founding member of both the IMF and the IBRD.

s: On whose ideas was the Bretton Woods plan mainly based?
o: John Maynard Keynes and Friedrich Hayek
Harry Dexter White and Milton Friedman
Harry Dexter White and John Maynard Keynes
x: The plan was built on the ideas of Harry Dexter White and John Maynard Keynes.

s: On which date did the IMF begin its operations?
x: The IMF was founded in 1944, came into formal existence on 27 December 1945 and began operations on 1 March 1947.

s: On which date did the IMF come into formal existence, with 29 members?
x: The IMF formally came into existence on 27 December 1945 with 29 members.

s: The Bretton Woods Conference of July 1944 was attended by delegates from how many allied nations?
x: 730 delegates from 44 allied nations attended the conference.

s: Which was the first country to borrow from the IMF, on 8 May 1947?
x: France was the first IMF borrower, on 8 May 1947.

s: The Bretton Woods Conference was held at the Mount Washington Hotel in which US state?
x: The conference met at the Mount Washington Hotel, Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, USA.

s: When were the Special Drawing Rights (SDR), known as 'paper gold', created by the IMF?
x: The SDR was created in 1967-69.

s: The Smithsonian Agreement of 1971 widened the band of exchange-rate fluctuation to how much?
x: The Smithsonian Agreement replaced Bretton Woods parities and widened the band to 2.25%.

s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the IMF?
x: Project financing is the World Bank's job; the IMF promotes monetary stability, gives technical help and lends for BoP problems.

s: Which country alone holds a veto in the IMF through its voting share?
x: IMF votes follow quotas, and the US alone holds enough votes for a veto.

s: Which one of the following correctly represents the weights in the IMF quota formula?
x: The quota formula assigns weights of GDP 50%, openness 30%, variability 15% and reserves 5%.

s: Since October 2016, the SDR basket has consisted of how many currencies?
x: The basket has five currencies since October 2016: US dollar, euro, renminbi, yen and pound.

s: Which of the following is NOT an IMF lending facility?
x: Stand-By Arrangement, Extended Fund Facility and Rapid Financing Instrument are IMF facilities; political-risk guarantees are associated with MIGA.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the IMF?
o: The IMF is headquartered at New York
The IMFC advises the Board of Governors
Article IV consultations are annual bilateral surveillance of each member's economy
x: The IMF is headquartered at Washington D.C., not New York.

s: IMF quotas decide a member's financial contribution, its access to borrowing and which of the following?
x: Quotas determine contribution, borrowing access and voting power; they do not fix exchange rates.

s: After the quota reform effective 25 November 2024, what is India's rank by IMF quota?
x: India's IMF quota is about 2.75% (votes about 2.63%), 8th by quota.

s: Which country became the 191st member of the IMF on 21 October 2024?
x: Liechtenstein became the IMF's 191st member on 21 October 2024.

s: What is the IMF's regular review of each member's economy called?
x: Article IV consultations are the IMF's regular reviews of each member's economy; the others are lending facilities.

s: Which body advises the IMF Board of Governors?
x: The International Monetary and Financial Committee (IMFC) advises the IMF Board of Governors.

s: Which currency was added to the SDR basket in October 2016?
x: The renminbi joined the dollar, euro, yen and pound in October 2016, making the SDR basket five currencies.

s: Which of the following is known as 'paper gold'?
x: The SDR, created by the IMF in 1967-69, is called 'paper gold'.

s: During India's balance-of-payments crisis in 1991, approximately how much was obtained from the IMF and World Bank, contributing to the New Economic Policy?
x: India obtained about $7 billion from the IMF and World Bank during the 1991 balance-of-payments crisis, preceding the New Economic Policy.

s: What kind of loans does the World Bank generally give?
o: Emergency loans repayable within a year
x: World Bank loans are generally medium- and long-term in nature.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: IBRD – Loans to middle-income governments for infrastructure
x: The IBRD lends to middle-income governments for infrastructure; MIGA gives political-risk insurance and ICSID settles investment disputes.

s: Which World Bank Group institution provides political-risk insurance and guarantees for foreign investors?
x: MIGA gives political-risk insurance; IDA gives interest-free credits and grants, and IFC handles private-sector investment.

s: Which World Bank Group institution settles investment disputes and does not have India as a member?
x: ICSID settles investment disputes, and India is not a member; MIGA insures against political risk.

s: In which year was the International Development Association (IDA) established?
x: IDA was set up in 1960 and gives concessional loans and grants; the IFC was set up in 1956.

s: In which year was the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID) established?
x: ICSID was established in 1966, not 1976; IFC dates from 1956 and MIGA from 1988.

s: Which World Bank Group institution deals with private-sector investment and conceived the 'Doing Business' report?
x: The IFC (1956) handles private-sector investment and advisory work and conceived 'Doing Business'.

s: To whom does the IBRD mainly lend?
o: The poorest countries as interest-free credits
x: IBRD lends to middle-income governments; IDA gives interest-free credits to the poorest, IFC serves the private sector and MIGA insures political risk.

s: In which year was the International Finance Corporation (IFC) established?
x: The IFC, which deals with private-sector investment, was set up in 1956.

s: In which year was the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) of the World Bank Group set up?
x: MIGA, which gives political-risk insurance, was set up in 1988.

s: Masatsugu Asakawa, elected in December 2019, became the President of which institution?
x: Masatsugu Asakawa was elected ADB President in December 2019, in line with the tradition of a Japanese ADB President. K.V. Kamath was the first NDB President; the AIIB and IMF are headed by others.

s: Who was the first woman chief economist of the IMF (2019)?
x: Gita Gopinath became the IMF's first woman chief economist in 2019.

s: Who was the first President of the New Development Bank (2015)?
x: K.V. Kamath was the first NDB President (2015).

s: Who was the IMF's youngest chief economist, during 2003-06?
x: Raghuram Rajan was the IMF's youngest chief economist (2003-06).

s: Masato Kanda, from February 2025, is the 11th President of which institution?
x: Masato Kanda became the 11th ADB President in February 2025; the ADB President is traditionally Japanese.

s: Ajay Banga became the President of which institution in June 2023?
x: Ajay Banga has been President of the World Bank since June 2023.

s: Who is the Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund?
x: Kristalina Georgieva is the IMF Managing Director; Gita Gopinath was First Deputy MD.

s: Which post did Gita Gopinath hold in the IMF from January 2022 to August 2025?
x: Gita Gopinath, the first woman chief economist (2019), was First Deputy MD from January 2022 to August 2025.

s: At which summit was the agreement establishing the New Development Bank signed?
x: The agreement was signed at the 6th BRICS Summit in Fortaleza, Brazil, in 2014; it is associated with the Fortaleza Declaration.

s: Where was the 4th BRICS Summit (2012), at which the idea of the New Development Bank was mooted, held?
x: The NDB idea came at the 4th BRICS Summit in New Delhi in 2012; it began operations in 2015 with equal voting rights and no veto.

s: The New Development Bank froze Russia-linked operations in March 2022. What was Russia's shareholding in the Bank?
x: Russia was a 20% shareholder of the NDB, which froze Russia-linked operations in March 2022.

s: Where is the headquarters of the New Development Bank?
x: The NDB is headquartered in Shanghai, with regional offices in Johannesburg, Sao Paulo, GIFT City and Moscow.

s: The BRICS New Delhi Declaration (2026) noted that the Global North, with about 15% of the population, holds about what share of votes in the IMF and World Bank?
x: The declaration demanded quota and voting reform because the Global North, with about 15% of the population, holds about 60% of the votes.

s: Where is the New Development Bank's regional office in India located?
x: NDB regional offices are at Johannesburg, São Paulo, GIFT City (India) and Moscow.

s:
Consider the following statements about the New Development Bank:
1. Its founders hold equal votes and no one has a veto.
2. It is headquartered at Shanghai.
3. It is open only to BRICS members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the NDB is open to all UN members.

s: Where was the 16th BRICS Summit held in October 2024?
x: The 16th BRICS Summit was held at Kazan, Russia, in October 2024.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Asian Development Bank located?
x: The headquarters of the Asian Development Bank is in Manila, Philippines.

s: Which country is the second-largest shareholder of the Beijing-based Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank?
x: China is the largest shareholder of the AIIB and India the second-largest.

s: At whose initiative was the Asian Development Bank (1966) created?
x: ADB was created at UN-ESCAP's initiative, not UNCTAD's; India is a founding member.

s: Which are the two largest shareholders of the Asian Development Bank?
x: Japan and the USA are the largest ADB shareholders (about 15.6% each); India is 4th.

s: What is India's rank among the shareholders of the Asian Development Bank?
x: India is the ADB's 4th-largest shareholder (about 6.3%).

s: Which country is the newest member of the Asian Development Bank (2025)?
x: The ADB has 69 members; Türkiye joined as the newest in 2025.

s: The President of the Asian Development Bank has traditionally been from which country?
x: The ADB President has traditionally been Japanese, e.g. Masatsugu Asakawa and Masato Kanda.

s: How many members does the Asian Development Bank have?
x: ADB has 69 members: 49 from Asia-Pacific and 20 non-regional; Türkiye joined in 2025.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Asian Development Bank:
1. It was set up in 1966 and India is a founding member.
2. India is its largest shareholder.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: ADB (1966) has India as a founding member, but Japan and the USA are the largest shareholders; India is 4th.

s: When did the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank begin operations?
x: AIIB's Articles were signed in 2015 and operations began in January 2016; it holds an AAA rating.

s: Which country is the largest shareholder of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank?
x: China is the largest AIIB shareholder (about 26.5% of votes); India is second (about 7.6%).

s: Where is the headquarters of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank?
x: AIIB is headquartered at Beijing; Shanghai hosts the NDB and Manila the ADB.

s: How many approved members did the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank have in September 2026?
x: AIIB had 111 approved members in September 2026; the ADB has 69.

s: Which institution publishes the World Economic Outlook?
x: The World Economic Outlook, Global Financial Stability Report and Fiscal Monitor are IMF reports.

s: Which of the following pairs of report and institution is correctly matched?
o: Global Financial Stability Report – World Bank
x: The World Development Report is a World Bank report; Fiscal Monitor and the GFSR are IMF reports and Global Economic Prospects is the World Bank's.

s: To what level did the World Bank's Global Economic Prospects of June 2026 cut global growth for 2026?
x: The June 2026 GEP cut global growth for 2026 to 2.5%.

s: Which institution publishes the Human Capital Index?
x: The World Bank launched the Human Capital Index in October 2018 under its Human Capital Project.

s: The Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor is identified with which bank?
x: The corridor is identified with ADB; AIIB co-funds MUTP-III and NIIF Phase II, and the AP Disaster Recovery Project is with the World Bank.

s: Which bank funds the Andhra Pradesh Rural Roads Project?
x: The AP Rural Roads Project is funded by AIIB; the Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor is ADB-funded and the post-Hudhud Disaster Recovery Project World Bank-funded.

s: Which institutions fund Phase I of the Amaravati capital project?
x: The World Bank (IBRD) and ADB fund Amaravati Phase I with $800 million each ($1.6 billion).

s: Which institution funds the post-Hudhud Andhra Pradesh Disaster Recovery Project?
x: The AP Disaster Recovery Project after Cyclone Hudhud is World Bank-funded.

s: Which institution gave a $1.5 billion loan for India's National Green Hydrogen Mission?
x: The IBRD (World Bank) lent $1.5 billion for the National Green Hydrogen Mission.

s: How much did each of the World Bank and the ADB commit for Phase I of the Amaravati capital project?
x: The World Bank (IBRD) and ADB gave $800 million each, $1.6 billion in all.

s: Which round of GATT negotiations was the Uruguay Round (1986-1993/94), which led to the creation of the WTO?
x: The Uruguay Round was the eighth GATT round; it involved 123 countries and created the WTO.

s: Which GATT Article permits free trade agreements as exceptions to the MFN principle, if they cover substantially all trade?
x: GATT Article XXIV allows FTAs as MFN exceptions provided they cover substantially all trade.

s: The World Trade Organization was established on 1 January 1995 under which agreement?
o: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
x: The WTO was established on 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement after the Uruguay Round.

s: Where is the headquarters of the World Trade Organization?
x: The WTO is headquartered at Geneva, not Vienna.

s: Which WTO principle gives developing countries bargaining space in negotiations?
o: Voting weighted by share of world trade
x: The WTO follows one-country-one-vote with consensus, which gives developing countries bargaining room.

s: As of March 2026, the World Trade Organization had how many members?
x: The WTO had 166 members in March 2026, the latest being Comoros and Timor-Leste (2024).

s: Which two countries are the latest members of the WTO, having joined in 2024?
x: Comoros and Timor-Leste joined the WTO in 2024.

s: Who is the Director-General of the WTO, serving a second term from 1 September 2025?
x: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala began her second term as WTO Director-General on 1 September 2025, to 31 August 2029.

s: Pascal Lamy, a former Director-General of the WTO, belongs to which country?
x: Pascal Lamy is French and was earlier the EU Trade Commissioner.

s: Which WTO Ministerial Conferences are specifically associated with a breakdown of negotiations?
x: The Seattle Ministerial Conference of 1999 and the Cancún Ministerial Conference of 2003 broke down.

s: Which of the following WTO bodies is wrongly matched with its function?
o: General Council – Runs the WTO between Ministerial Conferences
Dispute Settlement Body – Deals with panel and Appellate Body rulings
Trade Policy Review Body – Highest decision-making body
x: The Trade Policy Review Body conducts periodic reviews of members' trade policies; the Ministerial Conference is the highest decision-making body.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the WTO Ministerial Conference?
o: MC13 was held at Geneva in 2022
It must meet at least once every two years
MC14 was held at Yaoundé, Cameroon, in March 2026
MC12 was held at Geneva in 2022
x: MC13 was held at Abu Dhabi in February 2024; Geneva 2022 was MC12.

s: Where was the first WTO Ministerial Conference (1996) held?
x: MC1 was held at Singapore in 1996; Seattle (1999) and Cancún (2003) broke down.

s: Which WTO body runs the organisation between Ministerial Conferences and also sits as the DSB and TPRB?
x: The General Council runs the WTO between MCs and also sits as the Dispute Settlement Body and Trade Policy Review Body.

s: Where was the WTO's 13th Ministerial Conference (February 2024) held?
x: MC13 was at Abu Dhabi (Feb 2024); MC12 was at Geneva and MC14 at Yaoundé.

s: The Dunkel Draft (1991), prepared under Arthur Dunkel, belonged to which round of trade negotiations?
x: The Dunkel Draft of 1991, associated with Arthur Dunkel, was part of the Uruguay Round.

s: Which GATT round was held during 1964–67?
x: The Kennedy Round ran 1964–67; the Tokyo Round 1973–79, Uruguay 1986–93/94 and Doha was launched in 2001.

s: In which year was the Doha Development Agenda, which later stalled, launched?
x: The Doha Development Agenda began in 2001 and stalled.

s: In India, which body handles anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard investigations under WTO rules?
x: The Directorate General of Trade Remedies handles anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard investigations in India.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Anti-dumping — Duties on goods sold below normal value
TRIPS — Minimum standards for all forms of intellectual property rights
TRIMS — Investment measures that distort trade
GATS — Subsidies that are prohibited, actionable and non-actionable
x: GATS deals with trade in services. The classification of subsidies as prohibited, actionable and non-actionable belongs to the SCM Agreement.

s: Which two agreements are identified as the only new WTO agreements concluded in the first 30 years of the organisation?
o: Trade Facilitation Agreement and Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
x: The Trade Facilitation Agreement and the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies are identified as the only new WTO agreements in that period.

s: Which WTO agreement deals with trade-distorting investment measures such as local content rules?
x: TRIMS covers trade-distorting investment measures like local content; TRIPS covers IPR and GATS services.

s: Which of the following pairs of WTO agreement and subject is correctly matched?
o: TBT – Food safety, animal and plant health
TRIMS – Minimum standards for all IPR
x: GATS covers trade in services. SPS covers food safety and plant health, TBT technical regulations and TRIPS IPR standards.

s: Technical regulations and product standards that restrict imports are which type of trade barrier?
x: Standards and regulations, like phytosanitary conditions, restrict imports without a duty, so they are non-tariff barriers.

s: Which WTO agreement deals with food safety and animal and plant health measures?
x: The SPS Agreement covers science-based food safety and animal and plant health measures; TBT covers technical standards.

s: In which year did India enact the Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act to meet its TRIPS obligations?
x: The GI Act, 1999 was enacted to meet TRIPS obligations; the Patents Act was amended in 2005 for the same purpose.

s: What did the Doha Declaration on TRIPS and public health affirm about TRIPS?
o: Prevents members from regulating medicines in public interest
Must not stop members from protecting public health
Eliminates compulsory licensing by developing countries
x: The Doha Declaration of 2001 affirmed that TRIPS must not prevent members from taking measures to protect public health.

s: Which country joined India in proposing the COVID-19 TRIPS waiver in 2020?
x: The proposal (2020) came from India and South Africa, not Brazil; MC12 (2022) adopted a limited waiver for vaccine patents.

s: Section 3(d) of India's Patents Act, used as a TRIPS flexibility, is aimed against which of the following?
x: India used Section 3(d) against evergreening, along with compulsory licensing, as TRIPS flexibilities for public health.

s: In which year was India's first compulsory licence under its patent law granted, in the Natco-Bayer case?
x: The first compulsory licence (Natco-Bayer) came in 2012; the Patents Act was amended in 2005.

s: In which year did India amend its Patents Act to meet its TRIPS obligations?
x: The Patents Act was amended in 2005; the GI Act was passed in 1999.

s: At which WTO Ministerial Conference was a limited TRIPS waiver for COVID-19 vaccine patents agreed in 2022?
x: MC12 at Geneva (June 2022) agreed a limited waiver for vaccine patents.

s: Besides the e-commerce moratorium, what else lapsed at the WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference (Yaoundé, March 2026)?
o: The Peace Clause on public stockholding
x: Both the e-commerce moratorium and the TRIPS non-violation moratorium lapsed at MC14; no permanent solution on public stockholding was reached.

s: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, which box of support has no limit?
x: Green Box support is non- or minimally trade-distorting and has no limit; Amber Box support is capped.

s: Under the Agreement on Agriculture, what is the de minimis limit of trade-distorting farm support for developing countries?
x: De minimis is 10% of production for developing countries and 5% for developed ones.

s: Where and when was the WTO Peace Clause shielding developing-country public stockholding agreed?
x: The Peace Clause was agreed at Bali in 2013; a 2014 decision extended it until a permanent solution.

s:
Consider the following statements about the WTO Agreement on Agriculture:
1. Amber Box support is trade-distorting and capped.
2. Blue Box support is Amber Box support with production limits.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Amber Box covers trade-distorting support such as price support and is capped; Blue Box is Amber support with production limits.

s: What is the main cause of the present crisis in the WTO dispute-settlement system?
o: The African Group rejecting all panel reports
The General Council refusing to meet between Ministerial Conferences
India withdrawing from the Marrakesh Agreement
The United States blocking appointments to the Appellate Body
x: The United States blocked Appellate Body appointments, paralysing the WTO’s two-tier dispute-settlement system.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about WTO disputes involving India?
o: The USA challenged the JNNSM solar domestic-content rules and India lost in 2016
The EU, Japan and Chinese Taipei won a panel against India's ICT tariffs in 2023
The dispute over India's export subsidy schemes (MEIS, SEZ) was brought by the EU
The panel in the export subsidy (MEIS, SEZ) dispute ruled in 2019
x: The MEIS/SEZ export subsidy case was brought by the USA, not the EU (panel 2019).

s: Who among the following brought the WTO case against India's export subsidy schemes (MEIS, SEZ)?
x: The USA, not the EU, challenged MEIS and SEZ; a panel ruled against India in 2019.

s: Besides Brazil and Australia, who among the following challenged India's sugar subsidies at the WTO?
x: Brazil, Australia and Guatemala challenged India's sugar subsidies; the panel ruled against India in Dec 2021.

s: Who among the following brought the WTO dispute over India's solar panel domestic-content rules under JNNSM, which India lost in 2016?
x: The USA brought the solar panels case; India lost in 2016.

s: India opposes bringing which of the following plurilateral initiatives into the WTO rulebook?
x: Investment Facilitation for Development, backed by more than 120 members, is a plurilateral initiative that India opposes bringing into the WTO rulebook.

s: On which date did the WTO moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions lapse?
x: The moratorium lapsed on 31 March 2026 after MC14 failed to extend it; 66 members then signed a plurilateral agreement banning such duties.

s: India's core demand in the WTO food-security negotiations is a permanent solution for which issue?
x: India's core food-security demand is a permanent solution for public stockholding (PSH).

s: At the WTO, the US wants to deny Special and Differential Treatment to China, India, Brazil and which other country?
x: The US wants to deny SDT to China, India, Brazil and Indonesia; India defends SDT.

s: Since which year had the WTO moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions been in force?
x: The e-commerce moratorium ran from 1998 until it lapsed on 31 March 2026.

s: What does Phase 2 of the WTO fisheries subsidies negotiations, unresolved at MC14, deal with?
x: Fisheries Phase 2 deals with overcapacity and overfishing and was unresolved at MC14.

s: Non-tariff barrier codes are associated with which GATT round?
x: Non-tariff barrier codes came from the Tokyo Round; the Uruguay Round produced TRIPS, GATS and the Agreement on Agriculture.

s: The first Anti-Dumping Code was an outcome of which GATT round?
x: The Kennedy Round (1964-67) produced tariff cuts and the first Anti-Dumping Code.

s: About how many countries took part in the Uruguay Round of trade negotiations?
x: The Uruguay Round (1986-93/94) had 123 countries and led to the WTO.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Council of Europe, founded in 1949?
x: The Council of Europe sits at Strasbourg; Brussels is the seat of the EU.

s: Which country was expelled from the Council of Europe in March 2022?
x: Russia was expelled from the Council of Europe, which had 47 members in 2019, in March 2022.

s: Under the Treaty of Rome, 1957, which forerunner of the European Union was set up?
x: The Treaty of Rome (1957) set up the European Economic Community (EEC), the forerunner of the EU formed under the Maastricht Treaty.

s: How many member states did the Council of Europe have in 2019?
x: The Council of Europe (Strasbourg, 1949) had 47 members in 2019; Russia was expelled in March 2022.

s: Which treaty of 1992 created the European Union?
x: The EU was founded by the Maastricht Treaty (1992, in force 1993); the Treaty of Rome (1957) set up the EEC.

s: Brexit, the United Kingdom's withdrawal from the European Union, was carried out under which Article of the Treaty on European Union?
x: Article 50 TEU is the EU's exit clause; it was invoked for Brexit and the UK left on 31 January 2020.

s: Which country was the latest to join the European Union?
x: Croatia was the last country to join the European Union, in 2013.

s: In which year did the European Union adopt the Digital Single Market Strategy?
x: The EU adopted the Digital Single Market Strategy on 6 May 2015, with three pillars including better access to digital goods and services.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Council of Europe?
o: It is a body of the European Union
Russia was expelled from it in March 2022
x: The Council of Europe is separate from the EU; it is based at Strasbourg and was founded in 1949.

s: Under the India-EU FTA of 2026, the EU made commitments in how many services subsectors?
x: In the India-EU FTA (2026), the EU made commitments in 144 services subsectors.

s: On which date did the United Kingdom leave the European Union?
x: Using Article 50 TEU, the UK left the EU on 31 January 2020, bringing the EU back to 27.

s: Which one of the following organisations was established through the Bangkok Declaration of 1967?
x: ASEAN was established in 1967 through the Bangkok Declaration.

s: With the admission of Timor-Leste in 2025, how many members does ASEAN have?
x: Timor-Leste joined ASEAN in 2025, taking its membership to 11.

s: Where is the ASEAN Secretariat located?
x: ASEAN, set up by the Bangkok Declaration of 1967, has its Secretariat at Jakarta.

s: Which is the only ASEAN country that shares a land border with India?
x: Myanmar is the only ASEAN country sharing a land border with India.

s: Which of the following is a member of the Mekong Ganga Cooperation?
x: The Mekong Ganga Cooperation has six members: India, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam.

s: Which declaration was adopted at the 20th East Asia Summit held at Kuala Lumpur in 2025?
x: The 20th East Asia Summit adopted the Kuala Lumpur Declaration in 2025.

s: In which year did India become a summit-level partner of ASEAN?
x: India became a sectoral partner in 1992, full dialogue partner in 1996, summit-level partner in 2002 and Comprehensive Strategic Partner in 2022.

s: In which year did India opt out of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership?
x: India opted out of RCEP in 2019.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: ASEAN-India FTA in goods came into force – 2019
Review India sought at the 32nd ARF (2025) – RCEP review
x: The ARF dates from 1994. AIFTA (goods) came into force in 2010, India opted out of RCEP in 2019, and India sought early completion of the AITIGA review.

s: The East Asia Summit, founded at Kuala Lumpur in 2005, has how many members?
x: The EAS has 19 members: 11 ASEAN states plus India, China, Japan, the US, Russia, Australia, New Zealand and South Korea.

s: In which year were India-ASEAN relations raised to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership?
x: India became a sectoral partner in 1992, full dialogue partner in 1996, summit-level partner in 2002 and a Comprehensive Strategic Partner in 2022.

s: In which year was the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) set up?
x: The ASEAN Regional Forum dates from 1994.

s: In which year did India become a sectoral dialogue partner of ASEAN?
x: India became a sectoral dialogue partner in 1992, full dialogue partner in 1996 and summit-level partner in 2002.

s: The Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), signed in 2020, covers about what share of the world's population?
x: RCEP (ten ASEAN states plus Australia, China, Japan, New Zealand and Korea) covers about 30% of world population.

s: Where was the Mekong Ganga Cooperation launched on 10 November 2000?
x: The MGC was launched at Vientiane, Laos, through the Vientiane Declaration of November 2000.

s: Where was the 21st ASEAN-India Summit held in October 2024?
x: The 21st ASEAN-India Summit (October 2024) was held at Vientiane, Laos, which had also hosted the 14th in 2016.

s: Which of the following is NOT an area of cooperation of the Mekong Ganga Cooperation?
x: MGC cooperation covers tourism, culture, education, and transport and communications, not defence.

s: Who is the Secretary-General of the Commonwealth?
x: Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey of Ghana is the Secretary-General of the Commonwealth, headquartered in London.

s: Which country became the 32nd member of NATO on 7 March 2024?
x: Sweden became NATO's 32nd member in March 2024; Finland was 31st (2023) and North Macedonia 30th (2020).

s: In which year did the USMCA, comprising the USA, Mexico and Canada, replace NAFTA?
x: The USMCA replaced NAFTA in 2020; its first joint review was in July 2026.

s: Which country became the 30th member of NATO in March 2020?
x: North Macedonia became NATO's 30th member on 27 March 2020; Finland (31st) and Sweden (32nd) followed.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The SAARC Charter was signed at Dhaka.
2. The SAARC Secretariat is located at Dhaka.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Charter was signed at Dhaka (1985), but the Secretariat is at Kathmandu.

s: How many members does SAARC have?
x: SAARC comprises eight members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

s: Which one of the following is NOT an observer of SAARC?
x: SAARC's observers include China, Japan, the USA, the EU and Iran. Russia is not a SAARC observer.

s: Which land neighbours of India are not members of SAARC?
x: Of India's land neighbours only China and Myanmar are outside SAARC; Bhutan, Nepal and Bangladesh are members.

s: Which signatory has not ratified the BBIN Motor Vehicles Agreement signed at Thimphu in 2015?
x: The BBIN MVA was signed by Bangladesh, Bhutan, India and Nepal at Thimphu in 2015, but Bhutan has not ratified it.

s: The 19th SAARC Summit, scheduled at Islamabad in 2016, was cancelled after which of the following?
x: The 19th SAARC Summit at Islamabad was cancelled after the Uri attack. The 18th Summit at Kathmandu in 2014 remains the last summit.

s: Where is the SAARC Development Fund located?
x: The SAARC Development Fund is at Thimphu; Kathmandu hosts the SAARC Secretariat.

s: When did the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA), which replaced SAPTA, come into force?
x: SAFTA was signed in 2004 and came into force on 1 January 2006, replacing SAPTA.

s: In which year did Afghanistan become the eighth member of SAARC at the 14th SAARC Summit?
x: Afghanistan joined SAARC at the 14th Summit in April 2007, after the seven founders of 1985.

s: Where was the 18th SAARC Summit of 2014, the last one held so far, held?
x: The last SAARC Summit was the 18th at Kathmandu in 2014; the 19th at Islamabad (2016) was cancelled.

s: Which of the following was proposed by India in SAARC in 2017?
x: India's SAARC proposals include the South Asia Satellite (2017) and a COVID emergency fund (2020).

s: Which country hosted the 31st SAARC Council of Ministers meeting in February 2009?
x: The 31st SAARC Council of Ministers met in Sri Lanka in February 2009.

s: Where was the SAARC Charter signed in December 1985?
x: The SAARC Charter was signed at Dhaka on 8 December 1985; the Secretariat is at Kathmandu.

s: Which of the following was NOT a founder member of SAARC?
x: SAARC had seven founders; Afghanistan joined later, at the 14th Summit in 2007, as the eighth member.

s: In which year was the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement signed?
x: SAFTA was signed in 2004 and came into force on 1 January 2006.

s: Where is the headquarters of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation located?
x: The SAARC Secretariat is located in Kathmandu, while its Charter was signed in Dhaka.

s: Where is the Secretariat of BIMSTEC, set up through the 1997 Bangkok Declaration, located?
x: BIMSTEC originated through the 1997 Bangkok Declaration and its Secretariat is in Dhaka.

s: Which two countries joined BIMSTEC in 2004?
x: Nepal and Bhutan joined in 2004; BIMSTEC began in 1997 as BIST-EC with Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand.

s: At which summit was the BIMSTEC Charter adopted?
x: The BIMSTEC Charter was adopted at the Fifth Summit held at Colombo in 2022.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about BIMSTEC?
o: Each of its sectors has a lead country
Its sectors were expanded from 7 to 14
Myanmar earlier led the energy sector
x: BIMSTEC reduced its sectors from 14 to 7, not the other way round.

s: Where was MILEX, the first BIMSTEC army exercise (2018), held?
x: MILEX, the first BIMSTEC army exercise, was held at Pune in 2018.

s:
Consider the following statements about BIMSTEC:
1. It began in 1997 as BIST-EC.
2. Its sectors were expanded from 7 to 14.
3. India is the lead country for the security sector.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: BIMSTEC began as BIST-EC in 1997 and India leads security; statement 2 is wrong because sectors were cut from 14 to 7.

s: Where is the BIMSTEC Energy Centre, for which a Host Country Agreement was signed in November 2024, located?
x: The BIMSTEC Energy Centre is at Bengaluru; Noida has the Centre for Weather and Climate and Thimphu the Cultural Industries Observatory.

s: What is the full form of BIMSTEC?
o: Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Trade and Economic Cooperation
Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation
Bangladesh, India, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand Economic Cooperation
Bay of Bengal Institute for Maritime Security, Technical and Economic Cooperation
x: BIMSTEC stands for Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation; it began in 1997 as BIST-EC.

s: In BIMSTEC, India is the lead country for which sector?
x: BIMSTEC cut its sectors from 14 to 7, each with a lead country; India leads security (counter-terrorism, disaster management, energy).

s: Which country took over the chair of BIMSTEC in April 2025?
x: After the 6th Summit at Bangkok (April 2025), Bangladesh became BIMSTEC chair for the 2024-26 term.

s: Which agreement was signed at the 6th BIMSTEC Summit held at Bangkok in April 2025?
x: The 6th Summit at Bangkok adopted Bangkok Vision 2030 and signed the Maritime Transport Cooperation Agreement.

s: Where was the 1st BIMSTEC Youth Summit held in February 2025?
x: India hosted the first BIMSTEC Youth Summit at Gandhinagar in February 2025.

s: At which BIMSTEC Summit was the MoU for the Establishment of the BIMSTEC Grid Interconnection signed in August 2018?
x: The Grid Interconnection MoU was signed on 31 August 2018 at the Fourth BIMSTEC Summit in Kathmandu.

s: Which body was set up under the BIMSTEC Grid Interconnection MoU of 2018 to oversee its implementation?
o: BIMSTEC Centre for Weather and Climate
x: The 2018 MoU provides for the BIMSTEC Grid Interconnection Coordination Committee (BGICC) to oversee power-grid cooperation.

s: 'Bangkok Vision 2030' belongs to which regional grouping?
x: Bangkok Vision 2030 belongs to BIMSTEC; the South Asia Satellite and COVID emergency fund were India's SAARC initiatives.

s: The Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) is associated with which of the following organisations?
x: RATS is the counter-terrorism structure of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.

s: Where is the Secretariat of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) located?
x: IORA's Secretariat is at Ebene, Mauritius; Jakarta hosts ASEAN, Dhaka BIMSTEC and Riyadh the GCC.

s: Where is the headquarters of the African Union, which replaced the OAU in 2002?
x: The African Union (2002) has its headquarters at Addis Ababa; Strasbourg hosts the Council of Europe and Brussels the EU.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), set up in 1981?
x: The GCC, formed in 1981 by six Gulf states, has its headquarters at Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

s: Where is the Secretariat of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, founded in 2001, located?
x: The SCO Secretariat is in Beijing; its anti-terror body RATS is at Tashkent.

s: Who among the following was among the leaders behind the creation of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA)?
x: Nelson Mandela was among the leaders behind the creation of IORA in 1997.

s: How many members does the Gulf Cooperation Council have?
x: The GCC has 6 members: Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and UAE; Iran is not a member.

s: Which country is the newest member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation?
x: Belarus joined the SCO in July 2024 at the Astana Summit, making it the 10th member.

s: Which of the following pairs (meeting – venue) is correctly matched?
x: The July 2024 SCO Summit was at Astana; the 1st BIMSTEC Summit was at Bangkok, the 18th SAARC at Kathmandu and the 14th ASEAN-India at Vientiane.

s: Where did India and Pakistan become full members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation in 2017?
x: India and Pakistan became full SCO members at Astana in 2017.

s: NACIN Palasamudram in Rayalaseema serves as a regional training centre of which organisation?
o: UN Office on Drugs and Crime
x: NACIN Palasamudram is a World Customs Organization regional training centre for tax officials from SAARC, ASEAN and African nations.

s: From which country did India take over the chair of IORA for 2025-27?
x: India became IORA chair for 2025-27, taking over from Sri Lanka in November 2025.

s: Which of the following is NOT a priority area of the Indian Ocean Rim Association?
x: IORA's priority areas include maritime safety, trade facilitation, fisheries, disaster risk, academic cooperation and tourism; nuclear disarmament is not one.

s: Where was the last IORA Leaders' Summit, marking its 20th anniversary in 2017, held?
x: The 2027 IORA summit under India's chair will be the first since the Jakarta summit of 2017.

s: The Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), formed in 1997, has how many member states?
x: IORA, formed in 1997 with its Secretariat at Ebene, Mauritius, has 23 member states.

s: Where is the headquarters of the New Development Bank (NDB), established at Fortaleza in 2014?
x: The NDB was established at Fortaleza in 2014 and its headquarters is located in Shanghai.

s: What is India's position on de-dollarisation in the context of BRICS?
o: India backs an immediate common BRICS currency
India has made de-dollarisation a core foreign-policy aim
India has left BRICS over de-dollarisation
x: India avoids de-dollarisation even while participating in BRICS.

s: Who coined the term “BRIC” in 2001?
o: Amartya Sen of the United Nations
Joseph Stiglitz of the World Bank
x: The term BRIC was coined in 2001 by Jim O'Neill of Goldman Sachs.

s: Following the B-R-I-C-S rotation of the chair, which country chairs BRICS in 2026, after Brazil in 2025?
x: The chair follows the B-R-I-C-S order: Russia (2024), Brazil (2025), India (2026), then China (2027).

s: What is the theme of India's 2026 BRICS chairship?
o: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam – One Earth, One Family, One Future
Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability
x: India's 2026 BRICS theme is “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”

s: What is the size of the liquidity pool of the BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement, created in 2014?
x: The BRICS CRA (2014) has a liquidity pool of 100 billion dollars.

s: Where did South Africa first attend a BRICS summit as a member in 2011?
x: South Africa was invited in December 2010 and first attended as a member at Sanya, China, in 2011.

s: Which country joined BRICS in 2025?
x: Indonesia joined BRICS in 2025; Argentina, named in August 2023, later declined.

s: Which country, named a new BRICS member in August 2023, declined to join in December 2023?
x: Argentina was among the new members named in August 2023 but declined in December 2023.

s: Which grouping adopted the New Delhi Declaration of September 2026 seeking IMF and World Bank quota reform?
x: The 18th BRICS Summit at New Delhi (Sep 2026) adopted a New Delhi Declaration on UNSC expansion and IMF/World Bank reform; the G20 New Delhi Declaration was in 2023.

s: In which year was the first BRIC summit held at Yekaterinburg, Russia?
x: The first BRIC summit was held at Yekaterinburg on 16 June 2009 with Brazil, Russia, India and China.

s: Where was the BRICS Summit of 2024 held under Russia's chairship?
x: Russia chaired BRICS in 2024 and hosted the summit at Kazan; Brazil followed in 2025 and India in 2026.

s: How many members does BRICS have at present?
x: After its expansion and Indonesia's entry in 2025, BRICS has 10 members.

s: Following the B-R-I-C-S rotation, which country will chair BRICS in 2027?
x: The chair follows B-R-I-C-S order: Brazil 2025, India 2026, China 2027.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the origin of the G20 is correctly matched?
o: G7 summit that foreshadowed the G20 (June 1999) – Washington
Original G20 format (1999) – Heads of state and government
x: The first G20 meeting was at Berlin in December 1999. It was foreshadowed at the G7 Cologne summit, began as a finance ministers' forum, and leaders' summits started in 2008 at Washington.

s: Where was the first G20 Leaders' Summit held in 2008?
x: The first G20 Leaders' Summit was held in Washington, D.C., in 2008, in the context of the global financial crisis.

s: What does the G20 troika consist of?
o: The three largest economies of the G20
The current, previous and next presidencies
The G7, BRICS and European Union
The three permanent members of the G20 Secretariat
x: The G20 troika comprises the previous, current and next presidencies (B). In 2022 it was Italy (previous, 2021), Indonesia (current, 2022) and India (next, 2023). The G20 has no permanent secretariat, and the troika is not based on economic size or on G7/BRICS/EU.

s: Which body was admitted as a permanent member of the G20 under India's 2023 presidency?
x: The New Delhi Declaration (2023) admitted the African Union as a permanent member, the G20's second regional member after the EU.

s: What was the theme of India's G20 presidency, culminating in the 18th Summit at New Delhi in 2023?
o: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam – One Earth, One Family, One Future
Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability
Unity of voice, Unity of purpose
x: India's 2023 G20 theme was 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam – One Earth, One Family, One Future'; the third option is India's 2026 BRICS theme.

s: In 1999, the G20 was set up as a forum of which of the following?
o: Finance ministers and central bank governors
x: The G20 began on 26 September 1999 as a forum of finance ministers and central bank governors; leaders' summits began in 2008.

s: Which city hosted the G20 Summit in 2024?
x: The 2024 G20 Summit was held at Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; the 2025 Summit was at Johannesburg.

s: Which of the following is correct about the G20?
o: Its permanent secretariat is at Geneva
x: The G20 has no permanent secretariat or headquarters; it works through an annual rotating presidency.

s: At which venue was the 18th G20 Summit held in New Delhi in September 2023?
x: The 18th G20 Summit (9-10 Sep 2023), India's maiden presidency, was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.

s: Which countries formed the G20 troika in 2022?
x: The troika is the previous, current and next presidencies; in 2022 it was Italy, Indonesia and India.

s: Under the revised Brisbane-eThekwini Goal of the G20, the gender gap in labour force participation is to be cut by what share by 2030?
x: The revised Brisbane-eThekwini Goal (2025) aims to cut the gender gap in labour participation by 25% by 2030 from 2012 levels.

s: Which of the following countries is a member of the G7?
x: Japan is one of the seven G7 members, along with the United States, United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy and Canada. China, India and Russia are not G7 members.

s: After which event was Russia, which joined the group in 1997-98 to form the G8, suspended in 2014?
x: Russia's participation was suspended in 2014 after the Crimea crisis, turning the G8 back into the G7.

s: When and where did the G7 launch the Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII)?
x: The G7 launched PGII in Germany in 2022 as an infrastructure plan and a counter to the Belt and Road Initiative.

s: What is India's status in the G7?
x: India is not a G7 member; it is a regular outreach invitee.

s: Which grouping launched the Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII) in 2022?
x: PGII is a G7 plan launched in 2022 in Germany as a counter to China's Belt and Road Initiative.

s: In which country was the G7 summit of June 2026, where PM Modi met President Trump, held?
x: In June 2026 PM Modi met President Trump at the G7 summit in France; India attends as an outreach invitee.

s: BASIC comprises the three IBSA countries and which fourth country?
x: BASIC is Brazil, South Africa, India and China, while IBSA is India, Brazil and South Africa; China is the extra BASIC member.

s: Indonesia, which joined BRICS in 2025, is also a member of which grouping?
x: Indonesia is a member of BRICS (2025) and MIKTA, but not of the Quad or IBSA.

s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. G4 — India, Brazil, Germany and Japan
2. MIKTA — Mexico, Indonesia, South Korea, Türkiye and Australia
3. Quad — India, China, Japan and Australia
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. The Quad comprises India, the United States, Japan and Australia, not China; hence pair 3 is false.

s: Which one of the following groupings consists of India, Israel, the United Arab Emirates and the United States?
x: I2U2 comprises India, Israel, the UAE and the United States.

s: Which of the following is NOT a Quad initiative?
o: Indo-Pacific Partnership for Maritime Domain Awareness
x: The Quad initiatives include the Quad Vaccine Partnership, the Critical and Emerging Technologies group and IPMDA. The Contingent Reserve Arrangement is associated with BRICS.

s: How and where was the first Quad leaders' summit of March 2021 held?
x: The first Quad leaders' summit was virtual (March 2021); the first in-person summit was in Washington in September 2021.

s: The Quad originated as the Tsunami Core Group formed after the Indian Ocean tsunami of which year?
x: The Quad grew out of the Tsunami Core Group after the 2004 tsunami; it first met in 2007 and was revived in 2017.

s: In which year was the Quad revived?
x: After its first meeting in 2007 the Quad was revived in 2017; the first leaders' summit followed in 2021.

s: Where was the first in-person Quad leaders' summit held in September 2021?
x: The first Quad leaders' summit was virtual (March 2021); the first in-person one was at Washington in September 2021.

s: In which year was the Indo-Pacific Partnership for Maritime Domain Awareness (IPMDA) launched by the Quad?
x: IPMDA, a Quad initiative for maritime domain awareness, was launched in 2022.

s: BASIC was formed in 2009 before which international climate conference?
x: The BASIC grouping was formed in 2009 before the Copenhagen COP15.

s: Consider the following statements about IBSA: 1. It was founded in 2003 through the Brasilia Declaration. 2. The IBSA Trust Fund is managed by the World Bank. 3. IBSAMAR is its naval exercise. Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: IBSA was founded in 2003 by the Brasilia Declaration. Statement 2 is wrong: the IBSA Trust Fund (working from 2004, funds LDC projects) is run by UNOSSC, not the World Bank. Statement 3 is correct: IBSAMAR is the IBSA naval exercise, so the answer is 1 and 3 only.

s: Which principle does the BASIC grouping uphold in climate negotiations?
o: Uniform emission cuts for all countries
Exclusive reliance on private climate finance
Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC)
Carbon border taxes on developing countries
x: BASIC stands for CBDR-RC and climate finance from developed countries.

s: What is IBSAMAR?
x: IBSAMAR is the naval exercise of India, Brazil and South Africa.

s: Where was the IBSA Leaders' Meeting of November 2025 held, which said UNSC expansion is 'not an option but an imperative'?
x: The IBSA Leaders' Meeting of November 2025 was held at Johannesburg.

s: Which of the following is one of the five pillars of the Colombo Security Conclave?
x: The five pillars are maritime safety and security, counter-terrorism and radicalisation, trafficking and organised crime, cyber security and critical infrastructure, and HADR.

s: Which country is an observer, not a member, of the Colombo Security Conclave?
x: Seychelles is an observer; India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius and Bangladesh are members.

s: The Colombo Security Conclave began in 2011 as a maritime trilateral of India, Sri Lanka and which other country?
x: The Colombo Security Conclave originated in 2011 as an India-Sri Lanka-Maldives maritime trilateral.

s: In which year was the Colombo Security Conclave, which began as a trilateral in 2011, renamed CSC?
x: The India-Sri Lanka-Maldives maritime trilateral of 2011 was renamed the Colombo Security Conclave in 2020; its secretariat is in Colombo.

s: Where is the secretariat of the Colombo Security Conclave located?
x: The Colombo Security Conclave, renamed in 2020, has its secretariat at Colombo.

s: Where is the headquarters of the International Solar Alliance, launched by India and France at COP21 in Paris in 2015?
x: The ISA has its headquarters at Gurugram; CDRI is headquartered at New Delhi.

s: At which event did India launch the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) in 2019?
o: UN Climate Action Summit, New York
x: India launched CDRI at the UN Climate Action Summit in New York in 2019; its HQ is New Delhi.

s: When did India join the Minerals Security Partnership, a US-led grouping on critical minerals supply chains?
x: The MSP was formed in June 2022 and India joined in June 2023.

s: What was the theme of the first Voice of Global South Summit, hosted by India in January 2023?
o: One Earth, One Family, One Future
Unity of voice, Unity of purpose
x: The virtual Voice of Global South Summit (12-13 January 2023) had the theme 'Unity of voice, Unity of purpose'.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI)?
x: CDRI, launched by India in 2019 at the UN Climate Action Summit, has its headquarters in New Delhi.

s: What share of the world economy and population does the G20 account for?
o: More than 40% of global GDP, 46% of trade and 55% of population
40% of global GDP, 50% of trade and one-third of population
85% of global GDP, more than 75% of trade and two-thirds of population
20% of global GDP, 11% of trade and half of population
x: The G20 represents approximately 85% of global GDP, more than 75% of global trade and two-thirds of the world's population.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the share of the expanded BRICS grouping?
o: More than 40% of global GDP on a PPP basis and about 50% of the world's population
Exactly 46% of global trade and one-third of the world's population
About 85% of global GDP and more than 75% of global trade
About 20% of global GDP and 11% of the world's population
x: The expanded BRICS grouping accounts for more than 40% of global GDP on a PPP basis and approximately 50% of the world's population. The exact estimates vary by source.

s: Which of the following statements about the share of groupings in the world economy is NOT correct?
o: G20 accounts for about 85% of world GDP
G20 accounts for about two-thirds of world population
Expanded BRICS accounts for about 46% of global trade
Expanded BRICS accounts for about 50% of world population
x: The claim that BRICS makes up 46% of global trade is a wrong statement; the other shares are correct.

s: In 2011, BRICS accounted for 20% of world GDP but held only about what share of IMF votes?
x: In 2011 BRICS had 20% of world GDP but only 11% of IMF votes.

s: India is party to how many of the protocols of the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW)?
x: The CCW deals with inhumane conventional weapons, and India is party to all five of its protocols.

s: In which year did the United States withdraw from the JCPOA (Iran nuclear deal)?
x: The US left the JCPOA in 2018; the deal dates from 2015 and Iran dropped all limits on 5 January 2020.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. New START (2010) was a treaty between the USA and China.
2. The INF Treaty (1987) was concluded between the USA and the USSR, and the US withdrew from it in 2019.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: New START was between the USA and Russia (Russia suspended it in 2023). Statement 2 is correct: INF (1987) was a USA-USSR treaty and the US withdrew in 2019. So 2 only (B); A, C and D misjudge one of the two.

s: With which country did the P5+1 and the EU conclude the JCPOA in 2015?
x: The JCPOA (2015) is the Iran nuclear deal between Iran and the P5+1 with the EU; the US left it in 2018.

s: What is the full form of START?
x: START is the Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty; New START (2010) was between the USA and Russia.

s: The USA and Russia together hold about what share of the world's nuclear arsenals?
x: The US and Russia hold about 90% of global nuclear arsenals.

s: India's stated reason for not signing the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW) is that the treaty:
o: Adds nothing to customary international law
Is backed by all nuclear-armed states
x: India did not sign the TPNW and holds that it adds nothing to customary international law.

s: In which year did the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW) enter into force?
x: The TPNW, a binding treaty banning nuclear weapons, entered into force in 2021.

s: At which forum does India support negotiation of the Fissile Material Cut-off Treaty (FMCT)?
x: India supports FMCT negotiations at the Conference on Disarmament, for a treaty that does not cap existing stocks.

s: In which region did the Treaty of Rarotonga set up a nuclear-weapon-free zone?
x: Rarotonga covers the South Pacific; Tlatelolco covers Latin America, Bangkok Southeast Asia and Pelindaba Africa.

s: The Treaty of Pelindaba established a nuclear-weapon-free zone in which region?
x: Pelindaba covers Africa; Tlatelolco is Latin America, Rarotonga the South Pacific and Semipalatinsk Central Asia.

s: The Treaty of Tlatelolco established a nuclear-weapon-free zone in which region?
x: Tlatelolco covers Latin America; Rarotonga the South Pacific, Pelindaba Africa, Semipalatinsk Central Asia.

s: Which treaty set up a nuclear-weapon-free zone in Central Asia?
x: The Semipalatinsk Treaty covers Central Asia; the Bangkok Treaty covers Southeast Asia.

s: In which year was the NPT, which entered into force in 1970, extended indefinitely?
x: The NPT (signed 1968, in force 1970) was extended indefinitely in 1995.

s: India's principal objection to the NPT is that it:
o: does not contain any provision on nuclear energy
is discriminatory and perpetuates nuclear apartheid
recognises India as a nuclear-weapon state without conditions
x: India rejects the NPT as discriminatory, describing its structure as nuclear apartheid. India also seeks a time-bound disarmament plan from the nuclear powers before signing.

s: India has not signed the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) primarily because it:
o: lacks a time-bound disarmament commitment and permits subcritical tests
does not ban any form of nuclear explosion
x: India objects to the CTBT because it lacks a time-bound disarmament plan and still permits subcritical tests. The CTBT bans all nuclear explosions and was adopted in 1996.

s: In which year did North Korea withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT)?
x: North Korea left the NPT in 2003.

s: The NPT recognises as Nuclear Weapon States those that developed and tested a nuclear device before which date?
x: NPT NWS are the states that tested before 1 January 1967: US, Russia, UK, France and China.

s: How often are NPT Review Conferences held?
x: NPT Review Conferences are held every five years, and the consensus rule lets single states block outcomes.

s: In which year was the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) adopted?
x: The CTBT was adopted in 1996 and bans all nuclear explosions, but it is not yet in force.

s: Which of the following is wrongly matched?
o: MTCR – 1987 – Missiles and drones (500 kg over 300 km)
x: The NSG (1975) controls nuclear materials and technology; missiles and drones fall under the MTCR (1987).

s: The Hague Code of Conduct (2002) deals with transparency on which of the following?
x: The Hague Code of Conduct concerns ballistic-missile transparency; Wassenaar covers conventional arms and the Australia Group chemical and biological precursors.

s: Which pair of countries is outside both the Wassenaar Arrangement and the MTCR?
x: China and Pakistan are outside both Wassenaar and the MTCR; India is a member of both.

s: The MTCR seeks to control missiles and drones that can carry a payload of 500 kg over what range?
x: The MTCR threshold is a 500 kg payload over 300 km.

s: Which export control regime deals with conventional arms and dual-use goods?
x: The Wassenaar Arrangement (1996, Vienna) controls conventional arms and dual-use goods, not nuclear items.

s: The Australia Group controls the export of which of the following?
x: The Australia Group (1985) controls chemical and biological weapon precursors.

s: How many members does the Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR) have?
x: The MTCR (1987) has 35 members; the NSG has 48 and the Wassenaar Arrangement 42.

s: Where is the Wassenaar Arrangement, set up in 1996, based?
x: The Wassenaar Arrangement (1996), which controls conventional arms and dual-use goods, is based at Vienna.

s: In which year was the Australia Group, which controls chemical and biological weapon precursors, formed?
x: The Australia Group was formed in 1985; India became its 43rd member in 2018.

s: When did India join the Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR)?
x: India joined the MTCR in June 2016, the Wassenaar Arrangement in December 2017 and the Australia Group in January 2018.

s: India became the 43rd member of which regime on 19 January 2018?
x: India became the Australia Group's 43rd member in January 2018; it was the 42nd Wassenaar member in December 2017.

s: Which of the following export control regimes is India NOT a member of?
x: India is in the MTCR, Wassenaar and the Australia Group, but not the NSG; it has only the 2008 India-specific waiver.

s: In which year did India become the 42nd member of the Wassenaar Arrangement?
x: India joined the Wassenaar Arrangement as its 42nd member in December 2017.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India is a member of the Australia Group.
2. India is a member of the Nuclear Suppliers Group.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: India joined the Australia Group in 2018 but is not in the NSG; it has only the 2008 India-specific waiver.

s: In response to which event was the Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG) formed in 1975?
x: The NSG was formed in 1975, popularly known as the London Club, in response to India's 1974 Pokhran-I test.

s: The Nuclear Suppliers Group, a voluntary and consensus-based body, has how many members?
x: The NSG has 48 members; 35 is the MTCR's count and 42 the Wassenaar Arrangement's.

s: What does the India-specific NSG waiver of 2008, associated with the India-US Civil Nuclear Deal, permit India to do?
o: trade in civilian nuclear material and import uranium and reactors
join the NPT as a nuclear-weapon state
x: The 2008 waiver permits civil nuclear trade and the import of uranium and reactors by India. It does not make India an NPT member.

s: By what name is the Nuclear Suppliers Group also known?
x: The NSG, formed in 1975 after India's Pokhran-I test, is known as the London Club.

s: What mainly blocks India's entry into the Nuclear Suppliers Group?
x: The NSG works by consensus, so a single member can block India's entry; it has no permanent secretariat.

s: Under the FATF, a 'call for action' applies to jurisdictions placed on which list?
x: The black list covers high-risk jurisdictions subject to a call for action; the grey list only means increased monitoring.

s: Pakistan was kept on the FATF grey list from June 2018 to October 2022 mainly for failing to complete which of the following?
o: a 27-point action plan on terror financing
the IMF Extended Fund Facility conditions
its mutual evaluation under the Asia/Pacific Group
x: Pakistan stayed on the grey list (June 2018 to October 2022) for failing its 27-point action plan on terror financing. The other options are not the stated reason; the IMF EFF is unrelated to FATF listing and the APG is a regional body, not the cause of grey-listing.

s: In which category did India's FATF mutual evaluation, adopted in June 2024, place India?
x: India's mutual evaluation adopted in June 2024 placed it in 'regular follow-up'.

s: Which of the following countries is on the FATF black list?
x: The black list comprises Iran, North Korea and Myanmar; Monaco and Bulgaria were removed from the grey list and Pakistan left the grey list in 2022.

s: In which year did India become a member of the FATF?
x: India has been an FATF member since 2010; the FATF itself was set up by the G7 in 1989.

s: Which grouping set up the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) in 1989?
x: The FATF was set up in 1989 by the G7; its secretariat is at Paris (OECD).

s: Besides the FATF, India is a member of which FATF-style regional body?
x: India is in the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG), a FATF-style regional body.

s: Where is the secretariat of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) located?
x: The FATF secretariat is at Paris (OECD); Vienna hosts the IAEA.

s: In which year did India's Additional Protocol to its IAEA safeguards agreement come into force?
x: India's Additional Protocol came into force in 2014.

s: In which year did India join the IAEA as a founding member?
x: India joined the IAEA in 1957 as a founding member.

s: Which facilities are covered by the India-Specific Safeguards Agreement with the IAEA, signed in 2009?
x: The 2009 India-Specific Safeguards Agreement covers civilian facilities and excludes military ones.

s: Under a 2026 agreement, which country will supply India 10,000 tonnes of uranium during 2027-2035?
x: The 2026 India-Canada deal provides 10,000 tonnes of uranium (2027-2035) for PHWRs under IAEA safeguards.

s: Who is the Director General of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)?
x: Rafael Grossi is the IAEA Director General; he voiced worry over strikes on Iran's nuclear sites in April 2026.

s: Australia, with which India signed a uranium Administrative Arrangement in July 2026, holds about what share of the world's uranium?
x: Australia holds over one-third of world uranium; India and Australia signed an Administrative Arrangement in July 2026.

s: In which year did India complete the destruction of its declared chemical-weapon stockpile under the CWC?
x: India, a party to the CWC (in force 1997), completed destruction of its declared stockpile in 2009.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the OPCW?
o: It implements the Chemical Weapons Convention
It inspects the destruction of chemical weapons
It is an institution of the European Union
It received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2013
x: The OPCW is not an EU body; it implements the CWC, monitors the chemical industry and won the 2013 Nobel Peace Prize.

s: In which year did the Biological Weapons Convention, adopted in 1972 and to which India is a party, enter into force?
x: The BWC was adopted in 1972, entered into force in 1975 and has no verification organisation.

s:
Consider the following statements about the CWC and BWC:
1. The CWC came into force in 1997.
2. The BWC is verified by the OPCW.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The CWC was signed in 1993 and came into force in 1997; the BWC has no verification body, the OPCW serving only the CWC.

s: In which year was the OPCW awarded the Nobel Peace Prize?
x: The OPCW, headquartered at The Hague, won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2013.

s: Which of the following is NOT an organ of the OPCW?
x: The OPCW's organs are the Conference of States Parties, the Executive Council and the Technical Secretariat; a Board of Governors belongs to the IAEA.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW)?
x: The OPCW is headquartered at The Hague and implements the CWC.

s: Where is the headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) located?
x: The IAEA is headquartered in Vienna and was established in 1957.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) scheme was introduced in 2005.
2. The PIO card was merged into OCI in 2015.
3. Pravasi Bharatiya Divas has been held annually without a break since 2003.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: OCI was introduced in 2005. Statement 2 is correct: PIO was merged into OCI in 2015. Statement 3 is wrong: PBD, first held in 2003, has been biennial since 2015. So 1 and 2 only.

s: In which year did the L.M. Singhvi High Level Committee on the Indian Diaspora, set up in 2000, submit its report?
x: The committee was set up in 2000 and reported in 2002; it recommended Pravasi Bharatiya Divas, first held in 2003.

s: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas is observed on 9 January because Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa on that date in which year?
x: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas commemorates Gandhi's return from South Africa on 9 January 1915.

s: Who confers the Pravasi Bharatiya Samman, the highest honour for overseas Indians, at Pravasi Bharatiya Divas?
x: The Pravasi Bharatiya Samman is conferred by the President at Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.

s: Where was the 18th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (8-10 January 2025) held?
x: The 18th PBD was held at Bhubaneswar; Indore hosted the 17th, Varanasi the 15th and Gandhinagar the 13th.

s: Since 2015, how often has the Pravasi Bharatiya Divas convention been held?
x: PBD has been biennial since 2015.

s: Who among the following received the Pravasi Bharatiya Samman in 2015?
x: The 2015 Pravasi Bharatiya Samman went to Mala Mehta, Satya Nadella and Ashraf Palarkunnummal, among others; Ela Gandhi was not a recipient.

s: Who declared, on 8 January 2002, that Pravasi Bharatiya Divas would be observed on 9 January?
x: PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee declared PBD on 8 January 2002 after the L.M. Singhvi Committee report; the first PBD was in 2003.

s: Where was the first Pravasi Bharatiya Divas held on 9 January 2003?
x: The first PBD was held on 9 January 2003 in New Delhi.

s: Where was the 13th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas held in 2015?
x: The 13th PBD (2015) was held at Gandhinagar; PBD has been biennial since 2015.

s: The International Day of Yoga was established by a UN General Assembly resolution in December 2014. In which year was it first observed?
x: The UNGA adopted the resolution in December 2014 and the first International Day of Yoga was observed in 2015. 2014 is the resolution year, not the first observance; 2016 and 2017 are later.

s: Who set up the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) in 1950?
x: ICCR was set up in 1950 by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad; 1982 is the year of the first Festival of India, not of ICCR.

s:
Consider the following statements about Nalanda University:
1. It was revived under the Nalanda University Act, 2010.
2. Its new campus at Bodh Gaya was inaugurated in June 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: it was revived under the Nalanda University Act, 2010. Statement 2 is wrong: the new campus inaugurated in June 2024 is at Rajgir, not Bodh Gaya. So 1 only (A); B, C and D accept the wrong campus location or reject statement 1.

s: Which country returned the Leiden Plates, 21 copper plates from the time of Rajaraja Chola I, to India?
x: The Netherlands returned the Leiden Plates, 21 Chola copper plates of Rajaraja Chola I's time.

s: Which of the following is one of the four Ds of the Modi Doctrine?
x: The four Ds are Democracy, Demography, Demand and Diaspora; Development is not one of them.

s: In which country was the first Festival of India held in 1982?
x: The first Festival of India was in the UK (1982); the USA and France followed in 1985-86 and the USSR in 1987-88.

s: When was the UN General Assembly resolution establishing the International Day of Yoga adopted?
x: The UNGA resolution was adopted on 11 December 2014; the first Yoga Day was in 2015.

s: Jeffrey Armstrong was given which honour for 2021?
x: In July 2022 the ICCR named Jeffrey Armstrong its Distinguished Indologist for 2021.

s: Where is the new campus of Nalanda University, inaugurated in June 2024?
x: Nalanda University, revived under the 2010 Act, got its new campus at Rajgir in June 2024, not Bodh Gaya.

s: In which country was the Festival of India held in 1987-88?
x: The Festival of India began in the UK (1982), then USA and France (1985-86) and the USSR (1987-88).

s: What was the theme of the International Day of Yoga 2025?
o: Yoga for One Earth, One Health
x: The 2025 International Day of Yoga theme was 'Yoga for One Earth, One Health'.

s: Under the basic principles of UN peacekeeping, when may force be used?
o: In self-defence and defence of the mandate
To secure political compliance of the parties
To enforce a settlement without consent of the parties
At the request of the troop-contributing country
x: The principles allow no use of force except in self-defence and defence of the mandate; force for political compliance is not a principle.

s: Which United Nations body creates peacekeeping missions and ends them by resolution?
x: The UN Security Council creates and terminates peacekeeping missions through resolutions, while the Department of Peace Operations manages them.

s: Which UN department manages peacekeeping missions?
o: Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs
Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
x: The Department of Peace Operations manages UN peacekeeping missions, which are funded through a separate assessment scale.

s: Where is the Centre for UN Peacekeeping (CUNPK), run by the Indian Army, located?
x: CUNPK, New Delhi, trains over 10,000 personnel a year, about 2,000 of them foreigners.

s: In which country was the UN peacekeeping mission MINUSTAH deployed?
x: MINUSTAH was in Haiti; UNMIL was in Liberia, UNMISET in Timor-Leste and UNIFIL in Lebanon.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: MONUSCO — Democratic Republic of the Congo — 2010 onwards
x: MINURCAT operated in the Central African Republic and Chad from 2007 to 2010, not in Haiti.

s: India's first contribution to a United Nations peacekeeping operation was made to which mission in 1950?
x: India's first UN peacekeeping contribution was to the UN force in Korea in 1950.

s: India is the largest troop contributor to which of the following UN missions?
x: India is the largest troop contributor to UNMISS, with 1,775 personnel.

s: India was among the first countries to deploy an all-women Formed Police Unit to which country in 2007?
x: India deployed an all-women Formed Police Unit to Liberia in 2007 and was among the first countries to do so.

s: As of 2026, what is India's rank among troop contributors to UN peacekeeping?
x: In 2026 India is the fourth-largest troop contributor, with 5,200+ troops in 12 missions. Older questions (UPPSC 2011) keyed India as the biggest contributor, which is outdated; second- and tenth-largest are also incorrect.

s: In which country was the UN mission UNMISET (2002-2005) deployed?
x: UNMISET was in Timor-Leste; UNMIL was in Liberia, MINUSTAH in Haiti and UNMISS is in South Sudan.

s: Where is UNIFIL, a UN peacekeeping mission running since 1978, deployed?
x: UNIFIL is in Lebanon; UNDOF is on the Golan Heights, MONUSCO in DR Congo and UNMISS in South Sudan.

s: Which of the following was NOT a UN peacekeeping force?
x: The IPKF (Sri Lanka, Operation Pawan) was an Indian force, not a UN force.

s: India's largest contingent in UN peacekeeping history was in which mission?
x: India's largest contingent served in ONUC in the Congo (1960-64).

s: In which country was the UN peacekeeping mission UNMIL (2003-2018) deployed?
x: UNMIL was the UN Mission in Liberia, 2003-2018; India's all-women Formed Police Unit served there from 2007.

s: Which country hosts about 3.5 million Indians, the largest number of Indian nationals (NRIs) in any foreign country?
x: The United Arab Emirates had approximately 3.5 million Indians in the cited December 2025 data.

s: What was India's rank among the world's remittance-receiving countries in 2024?
x: India is the top remittance recipient, receiving about $129 billion in 2024.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian diaspora:
1. India received about $129 billion in remittances in 2024.
2. Indian-born people are now Australia's largest immigrant community.
3. The UAE hosts about 3.5 million Indians.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: India received about $129 billion in 2024, Indian-born people are Australia's largest immigrant community, and the UAE hosts about 3.5 million Indians.

s: In which year did the Government of Andhra Pradesh set up the AP Non-Resident Telugu Society (APNRTS)?
x: The APNRTS was set up by the AP Government in May 2016, under the chairmanship of the Chief Minister, to serve the Telugu diaspora.

s: In which country is the Salma Dam, an Indian development partnership project, located?
x: The Salma Dam and the Parliament building are in Afghanistan; Metro Express is in Mauritius.

s: When was the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) programme launched?
x: ITEC was launched on 15 September 1964 as a training-based capacity-building programme; e-ITEC is its online form.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the EXIM Bank of India is correctly matched?
x: EXIM Bank was established on 1 January 1982 under the EXIM Bank Act, 1981; its headquarters is in Mumbai, not New Delhi.

s: In which country is the Metro Express, an Indian grant project, located?
x: Metro Express and the Supreme Court building are Indian grant projects in Mauritius; Salma Dam is in Afghanistan.

s: For which region did India announce a $1 billion Line of Credit in 2020?
x: India announced a $1 billion Line of Credit for Central Asia in 2020.

s: Where is the headquarters of the EXIM Bank of India?
x: The EXIM Bank (set up 1 January 1982 under the 1981 Act) is headquartered in Mumbai and gives concessional Lines of Credit.

s: India built the Parliament building of which country as a grant project?
x: India's grant projects in Afghanistan include the Salma Dam and the Parliament building; Mauritius got the Supreme Court building and Metro Express.

s: From which country did India evacuate its citizens under Operation Kaveri?
x: Kaveri was the Sudan evacuation; Ajay was Israel, Ganga was Ukraine and Dost was the Türkiye-Syria earthquake relief.

s: For which of the following was Operation Dost (2023) India's relief operation?
x: Operation Dost was for the Türkiye-Syria earthquake; Maitri was Nepal, Kaveri Sudan and Ajay Israel.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Sankat Mochan (2016) was South Sudan; Ganga was Ukraine, Ajay Israel and Maitri the Nepal earthquake.

s: Operation Ganga (2022) was India's evacuation operation from which country?
x: Operation Ganga evacuated Indians from Ukraine in 2022; Kaveri was Sudan and Ajay was Israel (2023).

s: Operation Ajay (2023) brought back Indians from which country?
x: Operation Ajay (2023) evacuated Indians from Israel.

s: Operation Maitri (2015) was India's relief operation for which country?
x: Operation Maitri was India's relief mission after the 2015 Nepal earthquake.

s: Operation Vande Bharat (2020) was India's operation for which purpose?
o: Repatriation of Indians stranded abroad during COVID-19
x: Vande Bharat (2020) brought back Indians stranded abroad during the COVID-19 pandemic.

s: What does Vaccine Maitri, launched in January 2021, primarily refer to?
o: Programme for training foreign diplomats in India
Supply of COVID-19 vaccines to other countries
Evacuation of citizens from conflict zones
Financial support for overseas infrastructure projects
x: Vaccine Maitri refers to India’s supply of COVID-19 vaccines to other countries and was launched in January 2021.

s: Which was the first country to adopt India's UPI, in July 2021?
x: Bhutan was the first to adopt UPI (July 2021); Sri Lanka and Mauritius followed in 2024.

s: Which was the first European country to launch UPI, in 2024?
x: France became the first country in Europe to launch UPI, in 2024.

s: The Development Partnership Administration (DPA) was set up in which Ministry and in which year?
o: Ministry of Commerce and Industry in 2014
x: The Development Partnership Administration was established in the Ministry of External Affairs in 2012.

s: Which Ministry runs the Study in India programme, launched in 2018?
x: Study in India was launched in 2018 by the Education Ministry.

s: What is the online form of India's ITEC training programme called?
x: e-ITEC is the online form of the ITEC training programme.
